prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a person directly in front of the camera wearer beside a near-vertical rock wall, generally about 0.4–1.0 m away; the person and the camera wearer’s lower-edge hands are brighter than the wall, while the dark upper gaps and recesses are farther away. Across the strip, the person shifts from the lower-left/center to center, then toward the right and finally fills much of the right side, indicating decreasing distance and/or a rightward camera turn; the wall remains immediately ahead, roughly within 0.3–1.5 m depending on the protrusion or recess. The person’s raised arms and hands are above the torso and close to the wall, apparently within their arm’s reach, while the camera wearer’s visible hand in the last frame is also within reach of the person or backpack. The depth map makes relative proximity and the wall’s recessed cavities clearer than RGB alone, but its smooth, scale-free shading cannot support precise metric distances and appears unreliable at silhouettes, the image borders, and the dark overhead openings.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify one nearby person in every frame and a backpack on that person in frames 3 and 5; the person is left/center initially, centered in frames 2–4, and mostly on the right in frame 5, with the backpack behind the torso from the camera’s viewpoint. The person faces the rock wall and mostly away from the camera wearer, with arms raised above or beside the head; no clear face orientation toward the camera is supported, although a second partial profile-like region at the far left of frame 1 may belong to another nearby person roughly 0.5–1.5 m away. Person, backpack, and wall overlap strongly, showing that the torso occludes the backpack and that arms or body parts are sometimes cropped by the top, bottom, or side boundaries; the final frame brings the person and backpack close enough to occupy most of the right side, plausibly within the camera wearer’s arm reach. The map clarifies object extents and overlaps that blend into the RGB, but it is unreliable because rock is largely unlabelled, the large frame-1 “elephant” mask is clearly a rock false positive, some person masks merge with surrounding regions, and detections appear or disappear between frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it provides no detected body or hand joints, limb directions, facing direction, gaze direction, reach geometry, or motion across time. Consequently, it cannot independently locate the nearby person, the camera wearer’s hands, the backpack, or the rock wall, nor estimate distances or occlusions between them. Relative to the RGB, the missing skeleton is especially unreliable because the visible person has raised arms in every frame and visible hands or forearms in several frames, yet none are represented. Any spatial account of posture, arm’s reach, turning, or approach would therefore have to come from the RGB, depth, or segmentation maps rather than this pose output.
